Developed by UNA barbara e valentim, the project combines industrialized solutions with bioclimatic strategies - responding precisely to environmental conditions and the desire for a more landscape-integrated occupation.

title: The Carmine House / NPS Arquitectos
text:
The Carmine House / NPS Arquitectos

The property consists of a series of platforms that overcome the difference in height between the streets adjacent to the land (approximately 12 metres). On the upper level, there were already some buildings, which appeared somewhat fragmented. The proposal sought to unite these fragments, outlining a U-shape that defines a patio to the east and recovers the old threshing floor to the south/west. The ends of the new shape start at the pre-existing buildings and join to the west with a new body that, while maintaining its shape, stands out for its tectonics.

title: Zunli Tea House / OUT OF OFFICE DESIGN
text:
Zunli Tea House / OUT OF OFFICE DESIGN

Zunli Tea House occupies an old dwelling in Suzhou's historic Gusu district. The owner wanted to bring the intimacy and changing views of a classical Chinese garden into everyday domestic life. A modest budget, restrictions attached to the property's tenancy and the building's fragile condition set clear limits on the renovation. The original room arrangement had to be retained, opportunities for reinforcement were limited, and walls could not be cut into or chased for services. Electrical conduits were therefore surface-mounted, while furniture, planting and finishes became the principal means of reshaping the interior.

title: Fulldraw Winery / Clayton Korte
text:
Fulldraw Winery / Clayton Korte

Fulldraw Vineyard is located within the Templeton Gap AVA, the heart of California's Central Coast wine country. Set on 100 acres of established vineyards, the land is characterized by its rich limestone soils and cool maritime climate—the perfect setting for growing Rhone-style varietals. Tucked into the rolling terrain, the winery is accessed via a long, looping drive taking visitors through the vineyards before arriving at their destination. The proprietors, Connor and Rebecca McMahon tasked Clayton Korte with designing a winery that represents their personality and passion for winemaking. The solution is a winery that is familiar yet exclusive, comfortable yet sophisticated—seemingly disparate ideas that come together through a visitor experience that is as curated as it is intimate.

title: Central Kitchen Graz / Superfuturegroup
text:
Central Kitchen Graz / Superfuturegroup

The new Central Kitchen Graz combines the requirements of a large-scale food production facility with an architectural concept focused on sustainability, circular economy principles, and high-quality working environments. Approximately 15,000 meals are prepared and distributed to municipal childcare facilities and social welfare institutions every day.

title: Architecture as a Measured Intervention: Inside the Work of Atelier Guo
text:
Architecture as a Measured Intervention: Inside the Work of Atelier Guo

An architectural intervention is not simply a question of how much or how little to introduce, but of understanding precisely where and how to act. This precision begins with a careful reading of the existing context, including the recognition of the spatial, material, and environmental conditions that shape a place. It extends into the process of design and construction, where complex considerations are distilled into deliberate, coherent decisions. Rather than pursuing formal complexity or reduction for its own sake, a measured intervention seeks to establish a meaningful relationship between what already exists and what architecture can contribute.

title: Wujiaba Flight Path 1922 Park Pavilions / Potential Architects
text:
Wujiaba Flight Path 1922 Park Pavilions / Potential Architects

Wujiaba carries a century of Kunming's aviation memory. In 1922, Tang Jiyao established Yunnan's aviation force here and built what is widely regarded as China's second airport; it was also from here that Kunming residents first looked up to watch airplanes take off. During World War II, the airport served as a base for the Flying Tigers and a terminus of the Hump Route.

text:
How to Plan and Visualize For a City That Has Yet to Be Built

While most cities develop gradually, building one from scratch is hardly a new concept. Starting with a blank site, however, brings its own set of challenges. Rather than responding to an existing urban fabric, planners must anticipate how an entire environment will function, from its streets and infrastructure to its public spaces and the relationships between them.

title: Lisbon Triennale Announces CO-OP and Herzog & de Meuron’s Memphis Museum Opens: This Week’s Review
text:
Lisbon Triennale Announces CO-OP and Herzog & de Meuron’s Memphis Museum Opens: This Week’s Review

This week's news explores how architecture responds to collective needs, environmental challenges, and changing cultural contexts. From the Lisbon Architecture Triennale's announcement of CO-OP as the theme for its 2028 edition to the recognition of Mexican practice COLECTIVO C733 with the inaugural Siza Award for Public Architecture, questions of cooperation and the public realm remain central. At COP31 in Antalya, discussions on building energy efficiency and urban resilience brought the built environment into focus, while the 2026 World Architecture Festival recognized projects engaging with environmental performance across different scales. Meanwhile, new cultural destinations are taking shape in Doha, Memphis, and Tulsa, where museum and pavilion projects reconsider the relationship between architecture, art, and public space.

title: Bukhara Biennial 2027 Announces Theme and First Artists for an Edition of Lasting Public Works
text:
Bukhara Biennial 2027 Announces Theme and First Artists for an Edition of Lasting Public Works

The Uzbekistan Art and Culture Development Foundation (ACDF) has announced The Long Welcome as the theme of the second Bukhara Biennial, which will run from September 3 to November 21, 2027, in the historic Silk Road city. The biennial, conceived and commissioned by Commissioner and ACDF Chairperson Gayane Umerova, is led this time by Artistic Director Kulapat Yantrasast, founder of WHY Architecture. It follows the inaugural edition, curated by Diana Campbell under the theme Recipes for Broken Hearts, which opened in September 2025. Bringing together Uzbek and international artists, the biennial will present new commissions made exclusively in Uzbekistan, and it aims to leave a lasting legacy in the city through permanent projects, from artist-designed gardens and fountains to installations in restored historic sites.

title: Why Does the Same Floor Plan Get Drawn So Many Times?
text:
Why Does the Same Floor Plan Get Drawn So Many Times?

A floor plan arrives as a PDF. It shows the existing layout of a small store slated for renovation, and the client has sent it over the day before the first meeting. Before anyone can begin sketching a proposal, someone has to redraw the plan, line by line, in CAD. Once the ideas begin to take shape, the same space is modeled again in another program, this time in 3D, to produce images and renderings. The furniture list goes into a spreadsheet, the presentation comes together in a third program, and the client's comments arrive by email, text, and voice message, often with screenshots marked up in red, several steps removed from the drawing they refer to. If a wall moves after that, someone has to make the same change in each file.

title: Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest: The Contested Authorship of the World's Heaviest Building
text:
Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest: The Contested Authorship of the World's Heaviest Building

In the center of Bucharest, about a kilometer and a half from the Old Town, stands the world's heaviest building. The Palace of Parliament, the seat of Romania's legislature, occupies Dealul Arsenalului, a hill at the western end of Bulevardul Unirii. This straight avenue crosses the city centre from east to west for roughly three kilometers, passing through Piața Unirii, before ending in front of the palace's main façade, which rises 84 metres in stepped tiers of stone.

text:
Hill House / Taylor Knights

Hill House is a grounded, monolithic family home set atop one of Melbourne's prominent suburban ridgelines, overlooking Jells Park and extending toward the Dandenong Ranges. Conceived as a long-term, multigenerational residence, the project was driven by the client's desire for a home that could support personal life, professional activity, and evolving family needs within a single, cohesive architectural framework.

title: How Shipping Container Buildings Respond to Local Climate
text:
How Shipping Container Buildings Respond to Local Climate

Far from simply transporting goods from A to B, shipping containers have become a go-to building material across the US, forming the basis of everything from tiny homes to container pools, site offices to workshops. But given the size of the country, and the range of climates found within its borders, the approach to container architecture can vary significantly from state to state, even county to county.

title: BW House / Studio S+AO
text:
BW House / Studio S+AO

BW House is a renovated and extended residence designed by Studio S+AO as a private sanctuary within the city. Set on a 900-square-meter site, the house has a total building area of 1,500 square meters across three floors. Designed in an artistic modern tropical style, BW House combines minimalist architecture with a warm and contemporary character.

In this area, pressured by urban growth, tourism, and the tension generated by neighbors fighting to preserve their unique and picturesque informal homes, an opportunity arose in 2021 to embark on a complex journey through administrative procedures. This process was marked by clashes with disconnected government administrations and the defense of logic and coherence to carry out interventions on one of these peculiar properties.
